translation_en:
Li Jian 李堅 [registered in a civilian household of Tang County 唐縣, Nanyang Prefecture 南陽府, Henan; County School Student; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Jingyi 景義; second in seniority among brothers; age thirty-three, born on the first day of the fifth month]. His great-grandfather was Li Wenju 文舉; his grandfather was Li He 和; his father is Li Shi 實 [Department Magistrate of Zhaozhou 趙州]; and his mother is née Hao 郝. Both parents are living. His elder brother is Li Xian 賢; his younger brothers are Li Jin 謹, Li Yun 贇, Li Guan 貫, and Li He 賀; and he married née Guo 郭. He placed ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and one hundred and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yue Jian 越堅 [registered in a civilian household of Hezhou 合州, Chongqing Prefecture 重慶府, Sichuan; Directorate Student; specialized in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Zhigang 志剛; second in seniority among brothers; age thirty, born on the twenty-third day of the seventh month]. His great-grandfather was Yue Xing 興; his grandfather is Yue Daoming 道明; his father is Yue Yuan 源; his mother was née Su 蘇, and his stepmothers are née Liu 劉 and née Zeng 曾. Both his grandparents and parents are living. His elder brother is Yue Gao 高; his younger brothers are Yue Xiao 孝, Yue You 友, Yue Mu 睦, Yue Xian 嫺, Yue Ren 任, and Yue Xu 恤; and he married née Zhu 祝. He placed twenty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Ying 高瑛 [registered in a postal-relay household of the Juluo Postal Relay Station 聚落驛 in Shanxi, a native of Huangyan County 黃巖縣, Zhejiang; Directorate Student; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Tingbi 廷璧; third in seniority among brothers; age twenty-three, born on the seventeenth day of the sixth month]. His great-grandfather was Gao Geng 更; his grandfather was Gao Sishun 思順 [Registrar of Quanzhou Prefecture 泉州府]; his father is Gao Xin 昕; and his mother is née Zhu 朱. Both parents are living. His elder brothers are Gao Pei 佩 and Gao Qi 琦; his younger brothers are Gao Yan 琰 and Gao Lin 璘; and he married née Li 李. He placed fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Chun 張純 [registered in a civilian household of Tongliang County 銅梁縣, Hezhou 合州, Chongqing Prefecture 重慶府, Sichuan; Directorate Student; specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Weiyi 惟一; first in seniority among brothers; age twenty-seven, born on the nineteenth day of the third month]. His great-grandfather was Zhang Yuanyi 元一; his grandfather was Zhang Shengzu 勝祖; his father is Zhang Duo 鐸; and his mother is née Zhao 趙. Both parents are living. His younger brothers are Zhang Pu 溥, Zhang Han 瀚, Zhang Hao 浩, Zhang Jun 濬, Zhang Lan 瀾, and Zhang Cheng 澄; and he married née Ma 馬. He placed thirteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He placed thirty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefectural Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Zongyi; his grandfather was Minde [Assistant Magistrate (xiancheng) of Shaoyang County]; his father is Pu, his mother was née Cai, and his stepmother is née Zhou. Both father and stepmother are living (juqing xia); his younger brothers are Can and Sui, and he married a woman née Liang. He placed fifteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and one hundred and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Both his parents and grandparents are living (chongqing xia); he married a woman née Yan. Wang Hao 王豪 [registered under an artisan household in Jintan County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, Directly Attached (Zhili); student of the Directorate of Education (guozisheng); specialized in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); style name Renjie; fifth in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month]. title: 正統十三年進士登科錄
text:
皇帝制曰自昔君天下之道
莫要於內治之政修外
攘之功舉斯二者聖人
所以躋斯世於雍煕泰
和之域也夫修內治之
===
政必先於爵賞刑罰而
舉外攘之功必本於選
將練兵且爵所以待有
功必待有功而後爵則
天下有遺善刑所以待

translation_en: The Emperor's decree reads: "Since antiquity, in the Way of ruling All under Heaven, nothing has been more essential than cultivating the administration of internal governance and carrying out the achievements of repelling external threats. Through these two things, the sages raised the world to a realm of harmonious prosperity and supreme peace. Now, to cultivate the administration of internal governance, one must put first the bestowal of ranks and rewards and the application of punishments and penalties; and to carry out the achievements of repelling external threats, one must take as fundamental the selection of generals and the training of troops. Moreover, rank is the means by which one treats those of merit; yet if one must wait until there is merit before bestowing rank, then in All under Heaven worthy men will be overlooked. Punishment is the means by which one treats…

title: 正統十三年進士登科錄
text:
者食而戰則資於馬曰
將曰卒曰食曰馬四者
外攘所不可闕一也昔
之君子以謂將其卒則
選其卒之良戍其地則
===
用其地之人戰其野則
食其野之粟守其國則
乘其國之馬庶幾可以
百戰無殆不然則一郡
用兵而取給百郡非善

選其卒之良戍其地則
===
用其地之人戰其野則
食其野之粟守其國則
乘其國之馬庶幾可以
百戰無殆不然則一郡

translation_en: … strategy. Now, in a multitude of ten million, there must be one person of outstanding talent. Yet the wise and the foolish are intermingled, and peers are jealous and obscure one another's merits—how, then, can one recognize such a person of outstanding talent and promote him to the head of the armed forces? Among the people of a given region, there are garrison soldiers and there are farmers. Yet the garrison soldiers are not native inhabitants, and the farmers do not know martial affairs—how, then, can one rouse their valor and deploy them among the ranks of defense and guard units? text:

而充溢邊鄙歟朕祗承

為心而於安內攘外尤
加意焉子諸生學古通
===
今而來必深於其道矣
其具以對無騁浮夸務
陳切實朕將采而用之

translation_en:
…and the suitability for livestock pasturage differ in each place: how can one bring about their proliferation so that they fill the frontier regions to overflowing? We have reverently succeeded to the Great Lineage of Our Ancestors; Our heart is earnestly devoted to ordering the state and caring for the people as Our children, and We pay especial heed to pacifying the interior and repelling external threats. You scholars have come here having studied antiquity and mastered the affairs of the present, and you must be deeply versed in these principles. Set forth your answers in full: do not indulge in empty boasting, but strive to present what is pertinent and practical, and We shall select from your proposals and put them into effect.

Fifteenth day of the third month of the thirteenth year of the Zhengtong era [April 18, 1448].

title: 正統十三年進士登科錄
text:
彭時
臣對臣聞天下以一人為主一人君以一心為主
盖心者萬化之原萬事之本也大哉人君之一
心乎本諸心以安內則內治之政脩本諸心以
攘外則外攘之功舉尚何患乎賞善罰惡之不
得其當選將練兵之不得其宜而斯世之不躋
於雍熙泰和之域也哉大學以是心為家國天
下之本董仲舒以是心為朝廷四方之則其以
此歟欽惟
皇帝陛下稟聰明睿智之資備聖神文武之德誕膺
===
駿命嗣守
鴻圖臨御以来惓惓以經國子民為心先之以勵
精加之以恭儉其於安內攘外之道已無不盡
而見諸治效者亦已盛矣而猶不自滿足乃進

清問首舉爵賞刑罰次及選將練兵之事而責臣

陛下真大有為之君也可以為堯舜可以為禹湯文

彭時

臣對：臣聞天下以一人為主，一人君以一心為主。盖心者，萬化之原、萬事之本也。大哉，人君之一心乎！本諸心以安內，則內治之政脩；本諸心以攘外，則外攘之功舉。尚何患乎賞善罰惡之不得其當，選將練兵之不得其宜，而斯世之不躋於雍熙泰和之域也哉？《大學》以是心為家、國、天下之本，董仲舒以是心為朝廷、四方之則，其以此歟！欽惟皇帝陛下稟聰明睿智之資，備聖神文武之德，誕膺駿命，嗣守鴻圖。臨御以来，惓惓以經國子民為心，先之以勵精，加之以恭儉。其於安內攘外之道已無不盡，而見諸治效者亦已盛矣，而猶不自滿足，乃進臣等于廷，降賜清問，首舉爵賞、刑罰，次及選將、練兵之事，而責臣以切實之言。臣愚，有以知陛下真大有為之君也，可以為堯、舜，可以為禹、湯、文、武，可以隆太平之業於萬億年而愈盛矣。顧臣
translation_en:
Peng Shi 彭時

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that All Under Heaven takes the One Man as its master, and the One Man—the ruler—takes his single mind as his master. For the mind is the source of the myriad transformations and the root of the myriad affairs. Great indeed is the single mind of the ruler! When he roots it in his mind to pacify the interior, the administration of domestic governance is put in order; when he roots it in his mind to repel external threats, the achievements of warding off the outside are accomplished. What worry would there still be that rewarding the good and punishing the evil might not attain their proper measure, that selecting generals and training troops might not attain their proper suitability, or that this age might not ascend to the realm of harmonious flourishing and supreme peace? The Great Learning (Daxue) takes this mind as the root of the family, the state, and All Under Heaven, and Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 took this mind as the model for the court and the four quarters—was it not for this reason?

Reverently I reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor is endowed with the natural gifts of keen perception and profound wisdom, possesses the virtues of sagely divinity and civil and martial accomplishments, has grandly received the great mandate, and has succeeded to and guarded the vast enterprise. Since ascending the throne, you have been earnestly devoted to ordering the state and caring for the people as your own children, leading the way with vigorous diligence and adding to it reverence and frugality. In the way of pacifying the interior and repelling external threats, there is nothing you have not exhausted, and what has been manifested in the efficacy of governance is already magnificent. Yet you still do not feel self-satisfied, and have therefore summoned your servants to the court and graciously bestowed your pure inquiry—first raising the matters of ranks, rewards, and penal punishments, next touching upon the selection of generals and the training of troops, and charging your servants to offer practical and substantial words. Ignorant as your servant is, I have the means to know that Your Majesty is truly a ruler capable of great achievements: you can become Yao 堯 and Shun 舜, you can become Yu 禹, Tang 湯, Wen 文, and Wu 武, and you can exalt the enterprise of Great Peace for ten thousand times a hundred million years, growing ever more flourishing. Yet considering that your servant…

title: 正統十三年進士登科錄
text:
淺陋何足以奉
大對然罄一得之愚亦臣區區之素願也敢不俯
竭愚衷以少裨於萬一臣竊惟天生聖人而付
以君道之重聖人奉天而主宰天下之大內而
中國仰之以治外而四夷賴之以安則夫脩內
治之政舉外攘之功夫豈可以一日而或廢哉
然求其要不越乎爵賞刑罰選將練兵之二者
耳夫爵固所以待有功功者善之著於事也若
必待有功而後爵則天下之善未著於事者必
至於見棄何以使之皆知所勸而建功乎刑固
===
所以待有罪罪者惡之形於行也若必待有罪
而後刑則天下之惡未形於行者必至於茍免
何以使之皆知所懲而遠罪乎斯二者誠如
聖問之所諭也臣復奚言臣嘗竊觀唐虞三代之時
其賞善也有三德而曰宣者為大夫有六德而
曰嚴者為諸侯或俊乂之旁招或宅俊之克用
與夫賢能之賓興俊造之升進凡此皆不待有
功而後爵者也其罰惡也象刑以弼五教制刑
以教祇德或畔官離次之必誅或羞刑暴德之
必罰與夫左道亂政者刑之而不赦悖禮疑眾

punctuated:
淺陋，何足以奉大對？然罄一得之愚，亦臣區區之素願也，敢不俯竭愚衷，以少裨於萬一？

臣竊惟天生聖人，而付以君道之重；聖人奉天，而主宰天下之大。內而中國仰之以治，外而四夷賴之以安，則夫脩內治之政、舉外攘之功，夫豈可以一日而或廢哉？然求其要，不越乎爵賞刑罰、選將練兵之二者耳。夫爵固所以待有功，功者，善之著於事也。若必待有功而後爵，則天下之善未著於事者，必至於見棄，何以使之皆知所勸而建功乎？刑固所以待有罪，罪者，惡之形於行也。若必待有罪而後刑，則天下之惡未形於行者，必至於茍免，何以使之皆知所懲而遠罪乎？斯二者，誠如聖問之所諭也，臣復奚言？臣嘗竊觀唐、虞、三代之時，其賞善也，有三德而曰宣者為大夫，有六德而曰嚴者為諸侯，或俊乂之旁招，或宅俊之克用，與夫賢能之賓興、俊造之升進，凡此皆不待有功而後爵者也。其罰惡也，象刑以弼五教，制刑以教祇德，或畔官離次之必誅，或羞刑暴德之必罰，與夫左道亂政者刑之而不赦，悖禮疑眾…
translation_en:
…is shallow and crude; how could I be worthy of offering a grand reply? Yet to exhaust my humble understanding from a single insight has always been my modest, longstanding wish. How dare I not bow down and pour out my foolish sincerity, so as to be of some slight assistance in ten thousand?

Your servant humbly reflects that Heaven gives birth to the Sage and entrusts him with the weighty responsibility of the Way of the Ruler; the Sage upholds Heaven and presides over the vastness of all under Heaven. Within, the Central Lands look up to him for order; without, the four border peoples rely on him for peace. How then could the governance that cultivates internal order and the achievements that repel external threats ever be neglected for even a single day? Yet if one seeks their essentials, they do not go beyond two things: conferring rank and reward or punishment and penalty, and selecting generals and training troops.

Now rank is indeed meant to await those with merit, and merit is goodness made manifest in affairs. If one must wait until there is merit before conferring rank, then the goodness in the world that has not yet been made manifest in affairs will inevitably end up being cast aside; how then can everyone be made to know what encourages them to establish merit? Punishment is indeed meant to await those with guilt, and guilt is evil given form in conduct. If one must wait until there is guilt before inflicting punishment, then the evil in the world that has not yet taken form in conduct will inevitably end up escaping by luck; how then can everyone be made to know what warns them to stay far from crime? These two points are truly just as Your Sacred Inquiry has instructed; what more can your servant say?

Your servant has humbly observed how in the times of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, when they rewarded the good, those who possessed three virtues and displayed them became Grand Masters, while those who possessed six virtues and governed gravely became feudal lords; or men of eminent talent were summoned from all sides, or men of distinction were capably employed in office, along with the ceremonial recommendation of the worthy and able and the promotion of advanced scholars—all of these were cases of conferring rank without waiting for merit to be achieved first. And when they punished the evil, they delineated the statutory punishments to assist the Five Teachings, and instituted punishments to teach reverent virtue; or those who rebelled against their offices and deserted their posts were certain to be executed, or those who patronized criminals and practiced violent virtue were certain to be penalized, along with punishing without pardon those who used heterodox ways to throw governance into disorder, and executing without leniency those who violated ritual and sowed doubt among the multitude…

punctuated: 者，戮之而不宥。凡此皆不待有罪而後刑者也。然亦豈徒事乎爵賞刑罰而無其本哉？盖一本諸心而已矣。觀夫堯之兢兢、舜之業業，而懋敬於命德討罪之政者，其心為何如？禹之孳孳、湯之慄慄、文王之翼翼小心、武王之無作好惡，而克謹於彰善癉惡之事者，其心為何若？肆賞罰之有道，勸懲之有本，而下無遺善遺惡者，以此也。兹欲人皆遷於善，不待爵賞而自勸，臣願陛下心唐、虞、三代賞罰之心，使賞不徒賞，賞一人而千萬人知勸，則我朝賞善之典，與堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之所以賞善者同一揆矣，何憂乎天下之人之不皆遷於善哉？兹欲人皆遠於罪，不待刑罰而自懲，臣願陛下心唐、虞、三代罰惡之心，使罰不徒罰，罰一人而千萬人知懲，則我朝罰惡之政，與堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之所以罰惡者同一轍矣，何憂乎天下之人之不皆遠於罪哉？如是，則善者列爵而登庸，惡者率德而改行，禮義廉恥之行興，詭詐偷薄之風息，百官有濟濟之容，黎民有皥皥之俗，而雍熙泰和之治可躋矣。
translation_en: … executed without leniency. All of these were cases that did not wait until after a crime was committed to apply punishment. Yet how could they merely concern themselves with ranks, rewards, punishments, and penalties without having a fundamental basis? Indeed, it all stemmed entirely from the mind-and-heart! Look at the cautiousness of Yao and the wariness of Shun, who were earnestly reverent in their governance of appointing the virtuous and punishing the guilty—what was their mind-and-heart like? Look at the diligence of Yu, the trepidation of Tang, the reverent care of King Wen, and the impartiality free from personal likes and dislikes of King Wu, who were able to be prudent in the task of displaying the good and afflicting the evil—what was their mind-and-heart like? Thus, that rewards and punishments followed the Way, that encouragement and deterrence had a fundamental root, and that among those below neither goodness nor evil was overlooked—all of it was because of this. Now, if You wish for all people to move toward goodness and be encouraged of their own accord without waiting for ranks and rewards, Your servant wishes that Your Majesty take as Your own mind-and-heart the mind-and-heart with which Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties dispensed rewards and punishments, ensuring that rewards are not given in vain, so that by rewarding one person tens of thousands know to be encouraged. Then the institutions for rewarding the good in Our Dynasty will follow the exact same principles by which Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu rewarded the good. What worry would there be that the people of the world would not all move toward goodness? And now, if You wish for all people to keep far from crime and be deterred of their own accord without waiting for punishments and penalties, Your servant wishes that Your Majesty take as Your own mind-and-heart the mind-and-heart with which Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties punished evil, ensuring that punishments are not meted out in vain, so that by punishing one person tens of thousands know to be deterred. Then the governance for punishing evil in Our Dynasty will follow the exact same track by which Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu punished evil. What worry would there be that the people of the world would not all keep far from crime? If it is like this, then the good will be arrayed in rank and elevated to office, while the evil will follow virtue and reform their conduct; the practice of propriety, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame will flourish, while the customs of deceit, fraud, and frivolity will cease; the hundred officials will possess a dignified and stately bearing, the common people will enjoy contented and tranquil customs, and a rule of harmonious prosperity and supreme peace can be attained!

text:
□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□哉夫眾至
千萬必有一傑良將之有於世非果無也必欲知
其傑而用之臣願
陛下心唐虞三代選將之心而又精神以感召之氣
類以招徠之投之轇轕繁劇之地以觀其智置
之艱難險阻之中以觀其才則雖伯禹呂望召
虎方叔之流世不易得而凡才智出眾之士必
皆拔置於軍旅之上矣何憂乎智愚之混淆同
類之忌嫉哉一方之人有兵有農是蓋兵農岐
而二也必欲作其勇而用之臣願
===
陛下心唐虞三代練卒之心而又擇將帥以統之寬
雜征以恤之使三時務農以備衣食之資一時
講武以習攻戰之法尤於春蒐夏苗秋獮冬狩
之時益嚴夫簡閱練習之事則可驅列於禦衛
之間矣何憂乎戍非土著而農不知武哉至若
田有肥瘠之不同歲有豐歉之或異而兵食始
有不足之虞臣願
陛下體唐虞三代之心以足食為念而又擇人以督
耕屯使絕其兼并課其勤惰則可致其粒而積
貯於倉廩者陳陳相因矣雖古之委積以待軍

□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□哉？夫眾至千萬，必有一傑，良將之有於世，非果無也。必欲知其傑而用之，臣願陛下心唐、虞、三代選將之心，而又精神以感召之，氣類以招徠之，投之轇轕繁劇之地以觀其智，置之艱難險阻之中以觀其才。則雖伯禹、呂望、召虎、方叔之流世不易得，而凡才智出眾之士，必皆拔置於軍旅之上矣。何憂乎智愚之混淆、同類之忌嫉哉？

一方之人有兵有農，是蓋兵農岐而二也。必欲作其勇而用之，臣願陛下心唐、虞、三代練卒之心，而又擇將帥以統之，寬雜征以恤之，使三時務農以備衣食之資，一時講武以習攻戰之法；尤於春蒐、夏苗、秋獮、冬狩之時，益嚴夫簡閱練習之事，則可驅列於禦衛之間矣。何憂乎戍非土著而農不知武哉？

至若田有肥瘠之不同，歲有豐歉之或異，而兵食始有不足之虞。臣願陛下體唐、虞、三代之心，以足食為念，而又擇人以督耕屯，使絕其兼并，課其勤惰，則可致其粒，而積貯於倉廩者陳陳相因矣。雖古之委積以待軍
translation_en:
… [16 illegible characters] indeed? Now, in a multitude of thousands or tens of thousands, there is bound to be one outstanding hero; good generals do exist in the world—it is not that there are truly none. If one definitely wishes to recognize the outstanding among them and employ them, your servant wishes that Your Majesty would take as Your heart the heart with which Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties selected generals, and furthermore move and summon them through spiritual energy, attract them through shared affinity, cast them into tangled and demanding posts to observe their wisdom, and place them in the midst of hardship and peril to observe their talent. Then, although men of the caliber of Boyu 伯禹, Lü Wang 呂望, Shao Hu 召虎, and Fang Shu 方叔 are not easily found in the world, all gentlemen of outstanding talent and wisdom will certainly be selected and placed at the head of the military forces. What worry would there be about the confusion of the wise with the foolish, or jealousy and envy among peers?

Among the people of a region, there are soldiers and there are farmers; this is because soldiers and farmers have diverged into two. If one definitely wishes to rouse their courage and employ them, your servant wishes that Your Majesty would take as Your heart the heart with which Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties trained troops, and furthermore select commanders to lead them and relax miscellaneous levies to show compassion for them. Cause them during three seasons to devote themselves to farming so as to prepare the means of food and clothing, and during one season to practice martial arts so as to learn the methods of attack and battle; especially at the times of the spring, summer, autumn, and winter hunts, make the matters of inspection and drill ever stricter, so that they can be deployed into the ranks of defense and guard. What worry would there be about garrison soldiers not being local natives or farmers knowing nothing of military affairs?

As for the fact that fields differ in fertility and barrenness, and harvests vary between abundance and scarcity, so that military provisions begin to face the worry of insufficiency: your servant wishes that Your Majesty would embody the heart of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties by keeping sufficient food in mind, and furthermore select men to supervise the farming colonies, causing them to put an end to land engrossment and to assess diligence and idleness. Then grain can be procured, and what is stored up in the granaries will pile up layer upon layer, old upon old. Even the ancient practice of accumulating stores to await the army…

title: 正統十三年進士登科錄
text:
旅與夫倉積於豳粮峙於申者何以加焉土地
氣候之不齊監牧畜養之不力而馬政始有不
蕃之弊臣願
陛下法唐虞三代之心以息馬為重而又擇人以掌
監牧使之時其芻秣節其勞逸則可致其息而
充溢於邊鄙者千萬成群矣雖古之天閑十二
與夫思馬斯臧騋牝三千者何以過焉誠如是
則將皆智勇而無不良卒皆果敢而無不精食
皆充足而無不給馬皆蕃息而無或耗由是而
舉外攘之功有不戰戰必勝矣有不攻攻必克

和之治端在於

translation_en:
…troops, or the granary reserves at Bin and the provisions stockpiled at Shen—how could they surpass this? Because of variations in soil and climate, and laxity in pasturing and husbandry, horse administration has come to suffer from a failure to multiply. Your servant wishes Your Majesty to take as a model the mind of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, treating the breeding of horses as a matter of weight, and furthermore selecting the right men to take charge of the pastures. Cause them to supply fodder and grain at the proper times and regulate the horses' toil and ease; then they can be brought to multiply, and those filling the frontier regions will form herds of thousands and tens of thousands. Even the twelve imperial stables of antiquity, or the horses praised as "thinking of horses, and they were good" and the "three thousand tall mares"—how could they exceed this?

Truly, if this is done, then the generals will all be wise and brave without a single poor one among them; the soldiers will all be resolute and daring without a single unrefined one among them; food will all be abundant without any shortfall in supply; and horses will all multiply and thrive without any depletion. Proceeding from this to carry out the achievement of repelling foreign foes: we may choose not to fight, but if we fight, we will surely win; we may choose not to attack, but if we attack, we will surely conquer; we may choose not to defend, but if we defend, we will surely hold firm. We shall see the four barbarian peoples stand in awe and admiration, bowing their heads to the ground and declaring themselves vassals; the frontier marches will be free of the alarms of beacon smoke and battle dust; the common people will enjoy the peace of plowing their fields and digging their wells; and the governance of harmonious prosperity and supreme peace will truly rest in the present day! That is why cultivating the administration of domestic governance and carrying out the achievement of repelling foreign foes are things that cannot be neglected for even a single day.

Humbly reflecting upon our Dynasty, sage has succeeded sage, grandly planning for good governance. Grand Progenitor Emperor Gao received the Mandate of Heaven and founded the state; Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen accorded with the hearts of the people and pacified and cleansed the realm within the seas. Their way of domestic governance and repelling foreign foes…

陛下之策臣者臣既已略陳之而於終篇竊有獻焉夫
人主一心與天地同其量與日月同其明天地

punctuated:
垂裕後聖而無窮。仁宗昭皇帝溥惠澤以福蒼生，宣宗章皇帝奮德威以安夷夏，其內治外攘之道，仰紹前烈而有光。陛下纘承大統，丕闡洪猷，而於內治外攘之要，蓋已知之審而行之至矣。今又以策臣等，而必以尤加意為言，臣愚又有以知陛下留心於此，此即大禹不自滿假、文王望道未見之盛心也。
陛下之策臣者，臣既已略陳之，而於終篇竊有獻焉。夫人主一心，與天地同其量，與日月同其明。天地惟不息，故覆載而無外；日月惟不息，故照臨而不已。臣願陛下體天地日月之不息，心弘覆載照臨之盛心，執此之政，堅如金石，行此之令，信如四時，則宗社生民之福，必由此而愈盛；蠻夷戎狄之遠，必由此而咸服；三光六氣，必由此而順行；五嶽四瀆，必由此而奠位；動植之物、風雨霜露之所沾被
translation_en:
…bequeathed abundance to later sage-emperors without end. Emperor Renzong Zhao [the Hongxi Emperor] spread benevolent grace to bless the common people, and Emperor Xuanzong Zhang [the Xuande Emperor] roused virtue and majesty to bring peace to both non-Chinese peoples and the Chinese; in their Way of cultivating internal governance and repelling external threats, they looked up to continue the achievements of their predecessors and brought glory to them. Your Majesty has succeeded to the Great Lineage and grandly expanded the vast plan; as for the essentials of cultivating internal governance and repelling external threats, You have surely understood them thoroughly and practiced them to the utmost. Now You again question us, Your servants, on this in the policy examination, and insist on speaking of paying even greater attention to it. From this, Your foolish servant has a way of knowing that Your Majesty's mind dwells earnestly upon this matter—this is none other than the grand mind of Great Yu, who was never self-satisfied, and of King Wen, who looked toward the Way as though he had not yet seen it.

Regarding the questions Your Majesty has posed to Your servant, Your servant has already briefly set forth his views, yet at the close of this essay I humbly venture to offer a further word. Now, the single mind of the ruler of men shares the same capacity as Heaven and Earth, and shares the same brilliance as the sun and moon. Only because Heaven and Earth never cease do they cover and sustain all things without exclusion; only because the sun and moon never cease do they shine down without end. Your servant wishes that Your Majesty will embody the unceasing nature of Heaven, Earth, the sun, and the moon, and broaden in Your mind the grand intention of covering, sustaining, and shining upon all; that You will hold fast to these policies of governance as firmly as metal and stone, and carry out these commands as reliably as the four seasons. Then the blessings of the ancestral temples, the altars of soil and grain, and the living people will surely grow ever more flourishing through this; the distant Man, Yi, Rong, and Di tribes will surely all submit through this; the three luminaries [sun, moon, and stars] and the six atmospheric energies will surely move in harmony through this; the Five Sacred Peaks and Four Great Rivers will surely be settled in their proper places through this; all animals and plants, and all things moistened and touched by wind, rain, frost, and dew…

率稽首稱賀以爲堯舜之聖復見於
今日禹湯文武不得專美於前古
陛下億萬年之洪福與天地相爲悠久矣臣學不足
以知古才不足以通今芻蕘之言上瀆
天聽伏惟
陛下俯垂
睿覽則國家幸甚天下幸甚臣不勝悚懼之至臣
謹對
punctuated: 者，必由此而蕃庶；麟、鳳、龜、龍、膏露、醴泉，與凡休徵嘉瑞，必由此而畢至。將見四方萬國莫不相率稽首稱賀，以為堯、舜之聖復見於今日，禹、湯、文、武不得專美於前古，陛下億萬年之洪福，與天地相為悠久矣。臣學不足以知古，才不足以通今，芻蕘之言，上瀆天聽。伏惟陛下俯垂睿覽，則國家幸甚，天下幸甚。臣不勝悚懼之至，臣謹對。
translation_en: … will surely thereby flourish and multiply; the unicorn, phoenix, tortoise, and dragon, sweet dew and sweet springs, along with all felicitous omens and auspicious signs, will surely thereby arrive in full. We shall see the myriad states of the four quarters all leading one another to bow their heads to the ground in congratulation, deeming that the sageliness of Yao and Shun is seen once again today, that Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu cannot monopolize beauty in antiquity, and that Your Majesty's vast blessings for hundreds of millions of years will endure as long as Heaven and Earth! Your servant's learning is insufficient to know antiquity, and his talent is insufficient to comprehend the present; these words of a humble grass-cutter and firewood-gatherer ascend to importune the Heavenly hearing. Humbly hoping that Your Majesty will condescend to cast Your sagely gaze upon them, the state will be fortunate indeed, and all under Heaven will be fortunate indeed. Your servant is overcome with the utmost trepidation; Your servant respectfully replies.

title: 正統十三年進士登科錄
text:
臣陳鑑
臣對臣聞聖王以道治天下莫要於崇文德而
修武功盖文德莫大於爵賞刑罰武功莫重於
選將練兵文德崇而內治無不修之政武備修
而外攘無不舉之功然所以崇文德而修武功
尤在乎人君一心之運用也古昔聖王所以濟
斯世於雍熙泰和之域者又豈有外於此道哉
傳曰有文事者必有武備書曰祗台德先不距
朕行此之謂歟欽惟
皇帝陛下稟聰明睿智之資全聖神文武之德紹
===
祖宗之大統履九五之尊位道躋皇極盖已至矣而
望道未見之心常若有所未至世底隆平盖已
盛矣而視民如傷之念常若有所未及乃進臣
等於
廷降賜
清問而以安內攘外之道下詢芻蕘臣雖愚昧敢
不精白一心以對揚
聖天子之明命乎臣惟天佑下民而作之君聖人撫
天下而子乎民其所以經國子民之道莫□於

punctuated:
臣陳鑑。

臣對：臣聞聖王以道治天下，莫要於崇文德而修武功。盖文德莫大於爵賞刑罰，武功莫重於選將練兵。文德崇而內治無不修之政，武備修而外攘無不舉之功。然所以崇文德而修武功，尤在乎人君一心之運用也。古昔聖王所以濟斯世於雍熙泰和之域者，又豈有外於此道哉！《傳》曰：「有文事者必有武備。」《書》曰：「祗台德先，不距朕行。」此之謂歟！欽惟皇帝陛下稟聰明睿智之資，全聖神文武之德，紹祖宗之大統，履九五之尊位。道躋皇極，盖已至矣，而望道未見之心，常若有所未至；世底隆平，盖已盛矣，而視民如傷之念，常若有所未及。乃進臣等於廷，降賜清問，而以安內攘外之道下詢芻蕘。臣雖愚昧，敢不精白一心，以對揚聖天子之明命乎！臣惟天佑下民而作之君，聖人撫天下而子乎民，其所以經國子民之道，莫□於崇文德、修武功而已。盖爵賞刑罰，所□□□之
translation_en:
Your servant Chen Jian 陳鑑.

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that when a sage-king governs all under Heaven through the Way, nothing is more essential than exalting civil virtue and cultivating military merit. For in civil virtue, nothing is greater than noble ranks, rewards, and punishments; in military merit, nothing is weightier than selecting generals and training troops. When civil virtue is exalted, there is no governance in domestic administration that is not cultivated; when military preparedness is cultivated, there is no achievement in repelling external threats that is not accomplished. Yet the means of exalting civil virtue and cultivating military merit lies above all in the operation of the ruler's single mind. How could the means by which the sage-kings of antiquity brought this world into a realm of harmonious, tranquil, and supreme peace lie outside of this Way? The Commentary (Zhuan) says: "One who has civil affairs must have military preparedness." The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Reverently take my virtue as the priority, and none will resist my conduct." Is this not what is meant!

Your servant reverently reflects that Your Majesty the Emperor is endowed with a disposition of keen perception and profound wisdom, and possesses in full the virtues of sagely spirituality and civil and military accomplishment; You have succeeded to the great line of Your ancestors and occupy the exalted position of the nine-in-the-fifth. Your Way has ascended to the August Ultimate, which has indeed reached perfection, yet Your mind, longing for the Way as though not yet seeing it, constantly feels as if it has fallen short; the age has attained flourishing peace, which is indeed at its height, yet Your concern in looking upon the people as though they were wounded constantly feels as if it has not reached far enough. Thus You have brought Your servants forward into the court, graciously bestowing Your clear questioning, and condescending to ask humble woodgatherers about the Way of pacifying the interior and repelling the exterior. Though Your servant is foolish and ignorant, how dare he not purify his mind in single-hearted devotion to respond to and extol the bright command of the sagely Son of Heaven!

Your servant reflects that Heaven aids the people below and makes for them a ruler, and the sage pacifies all under Heaven and treats the people as his children; in his Way of ordering the state and treating the people as children, nothing is more [essential?] than exalting civil virtue and cultivating military merit, and that is all. For noble ranks, rewards, and punishments are the means by which [to exalt civil virtue?]…

title: 正統十三年進士登科錄
text:
而內治之政以修選將練兵所以修武功而外
攘之功以舉然必本於人君一心公足以服衆
則賞罰之道行而人心無不化明足以選將則
訓練有其方而封守無不固矣且夫功者善之
見於事善者德之蘊諸已者也爵固以待有功
苟必待有功而後爵則天下豈無遺善乎要必
惟德是爵而務合乎人心之公所謂爵人於朝
與衆共之則爵不及惡德而善者知所勸矣罪
者惡之巳著惡者罪之未形者也刑固以待有
罪苟必待有罪而後刑則四海豈無遺惡乎要
===
必惟惡是警而常存乎欽恤之心所謂刑人於
市與衆棄之則罰不及無辜而惡者知所懲矣
稽之於古周禮六德六行六藝以興賢能之類
則賞無遺善矣又豈必待有功而後爵哉王制
行偽而堅言偽而辨以疑衆殺之類則刑無遺
惡矣又豈必待有罪而後刑哉然皆本乎在上
之人一心之公有以運用於其間也今也必欲
人人皆遷於善不待爵賞而自勸臣願
皇上法帝舜知人之哲爵賞惟賢而惡德無以售其
私則人皆力於為善不待爵賞之施而自無不

translation_en:
…and thereby the governance of internal order is cultivated; selecting generals and training troops are the means to cultivate military achievements, and thereby the accomplishments of repelling external threats are realized. Yet this must be rooted in the single mind of the ruler: when his impartiality is sufficient to win the submission of the multitude, the way of rewards and punishments will prevail and the minds of the people will never fail to be transformed; when his discernment is sufficient to select generals, training will have its proper method and the defense of the frontiers will never fail to be secure.

Moreover, merit is goodness manifested in deeds, whereas goodness is virtue stored within oneself. Ranks of nobility are assuredly meant to await those with merit, yet if one must wait until there is merit before bestowing rank, how could the realm be without overlooked goodness? What is essential is to bestow rank solely upon virtue and to strive to accord with the impartiality of popular sentiment—what is meant by "bestowing rank upon men in the court, sharing it with the multitude"—so that ranks of nobility do not reach those of base virtue, and the good know whereby to be encouraged. A crime is evil that has already become manifest, whereas evil is a crime that has not yet taken form. Punishments are assuredly meant to await those guilty of crime, yet if one must wait until there is a crime before applying punishment, how could the Four Seas be without overlooked evil? What is essential is to admonish solely against evil while always preserving a mind of reverent compassion—what is meant by "punishing men in the marketplace, casting them out junto with the multitude"—so that penalties do not reach the innocent, and the evil know whereby to be deterred.

If we examine antiquity, in cases such as the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) promoting the worthy and capable on the basis of the six virtues, six conducts, and six arts, rewards left no goodness overlooked; why must one wait until there is merit before bestowing rank? In cases such as the Royal Regulations (Wangzhi) putting to death for misleading the multitude those whose conduct is deceitful yet obstinate and whose speech is deceitful yet specious, punishments left no evil overlooked; why must one wait until there is a crime before applying punishment? Yet all of this is rooted in the impartiality of the single mind of the one above having the means to operate therein.

Today, if we truly wish every person to move toward goodness and be encouraged of their own accord without waiting for ranks and rewards, your servant wishes that Your Majesty emulate Emperor Shun's wisdom in knowing men, bestowing ranks and rewards solely upon the worthy so that those of base virtue have no means to peddle their selfish interests; then all people will exert themselves in doing good, and without waiting for the bestowal of ranks and rewards they will naturally never fail to…

title: 正統十三年進士登科錄
text:
勸於善矣必欲人人皆遠於罪不待刑罰而自
懲臣願
皇上體虞舜好生之德漸涵浸漬浹洽於民之心則
人自不犯于有司不待刑罰之用而自無不懲
於惡矣至若將者所以統夫兵卒者所以用於
將而食則卒之所仰馬則戰之所資也兵非將
則渙散而無統將非兵則孤立而無助卒而非
食何以為生戰而非馬何以克敵欲舉外攘之
功於是四者誠不可以闕其一也昔之君子乃
謂將其卒則選其卒之良戍其地則用其地之
===
人戰其野則食其野之粟守其國則乘其國之
馬庶幾可以百戰無殆不然則一郡用兵而取
給百郡非善策者誠以將其卒而選其卒之良
則將識士情而士知將意故所向成功戍其地
而用其地之人則安於風土閑於練習故可用
其力戰其野而食其野之粟則可以免轉輸之
勞守其國而乘其國之馬則可以免調發之患
是惟不戰戰則必勝是惟不攻攻則必克矣設
使不然則一郡用兵而取給於百郡徒見其勞
費多而成功寡何在其為良策也哉

是惟不戰戰則必勝是惟不攻攻則必克矣設

費多而成功寡何在其為良策也哉
punctuated:
勸於善矣。必欲人人皆遠於罪，不待刑罰而自懲，臣願皇上體虞舜好生之德，漸涵浸漬，浹洽於民之心，則人自不犯于有司，不待刑罰之用，而自無不懲於惡矣。
至若將者，所以統夫兵；卒者，所以用於將；而食則卒之所仰，馬則戰之所資也。兵非將則渙散而無統，將非兵則孤立而無助；卒而非食，何以為生？戰而非馬，何以克敵？欲舉外攘之功，於是四者，誠不可以闕其一也。昔之君子乃謂：「將其卒則選其卒之良，戍其地則用其地之人，戰其野則食其野之粟，守其國則乘其國之馬，庶幾可以百戰無殆；不然，則一郡用兵而取給百郡，非善策者。」誠以將其卒而選其卒之良，則將識士情而士知將意，故所向成功；戍其地而用其地之人，則安於風土，閑於練習，故可用其力；戰其野而食其野之粟，則可以免轉輸之勞；守其國而乘其國之馬，則可以免調發之患。是惟不戰，戰則必勝；是惟不攻，攻則必克矣。設使不然，則一郡用兵而取給於百郡，徒見其勞費多而成功寡，何在其為良策也哉？
translation_en:
…encouraged toward goodness. If you necessarily wish for everyone to stay far from crime and restrain themselves without waiting for punishments and penalties, your servant hopes that Your Majesty will embody Yu Shun's virtue of loving life, gradually steeping and saturating the minds of the people until it thoroughly pervades them; then people will naturally not offend against the authorities, and without waiting for the application of punishments and penalties, there will naturally be none who do not restrain themselves from evil.

As for generals, they are the means by which troops are commanded; soldiers are the means by which generals are served; food is what soldiers rely upon; and horses are what warfare depends upon. Without a general, troops are scattered and without command; without troops, a general stands isolated and without assistance. If soldiers lack food, how can they survive? If warfare lacks horses, how can the enemy be overcome? In wishing to achieve the merit of repelling external threats, among these four things, truly not a single one can be lacking. A gentleman of old once said that to command the soldiers by selecting the best among those very soldiers, to garrison a region by employing the people of that very region, to fight in the field by eating the grain of that very field, and to defend a domain by riding the horses of that very domain—by doing so, one may perhaps fight a hundred battles without peril; otherwise, employing troops in one commandery while drawing supplies from a hundred commanderies is not a sound strategy. Truly, this is because when commanding the soldiers by selecting the best among those very soldiers, the general knows the feelings of the men and the men understand the intentions of the general, and therefore wherever they turn they achieve success; when garrisoning a region by employing the people of that very region, they are accustomed to the local environment and climate and skilled in their training, and therefore their strength can be put to use; when fighting in the field by eating the grain of that very field, the toil of transport can be avoided; and when defending a domain by riding the horses of that very domain, the trouble of requisitioning and dispatching mounts can be avoided. Thus, only if one does not fight—for if one fights, one will certainly win; only if one does not attack—for if one attacks, one will certainly conquer. Suppose it were not so, and when one commandery employed troops it drew its supplies from a hundred commanderies: one would merely see much toil and expense with little success achieved—how could that be considered a sound strategy?

title: 正統十三年進士登科錄
text:
皇上又慮眾至千萬必有一傑然智愚混淆同類忌
蔽何以能知其傑而拔置軍旅之上者臣愚以
為果有超出萬人之才而謂之傑者出於萬眾
之中苟能察而知之則雖或混淆於智愚自不
能掩其賢雖為同類所忌蔽自不能沒其善於
是舉而授以將帥之任信而用之俾統軍旅之
眾將見如古屠販之流皆得起而為名將何患
將帥之不得其人哉
皇上又慮戍非土著農不知武何以能作其勇而驅
列禦衞之間者臣愚以為戍者雖非土著然習
===
染既久亦自便於風土農者雖不知武然訓練

Your Majesty is also concerned: "Among a multitude reaching thousands or tens of thousands, there must be a hero; yet when the wise and the foolish are mingled together and peers jealously obscure one another, how can one recognize that hero and promote him to the head of the military forces?" Your foolish servant considers that if there truly is someone of talent surpassing ten thousand men—who may be called a hero—emerging from among the myriad multitude, so long as one can examine and recognize him, then even if he is mingled among the wise and the foolish, his worthiness naturally cannot be concealed; and even if he is jealously obscured by his peers, his excellence naturally cannot be obliterated. Thereupon, if you elevate him and entrust him with the responsibility of a commander, trust him and employ him, and cause him to command the multitude of the military forces, we shall see men like the butchers and peddlers of antiquity all able to rise up and become famous generals. Why worry that we will not find the right men for commanders?

Your Majesty is also concerned: "Garrison troops are not natives of the soil, and farmers do not know martial arts; how can one rouse their courage and deploy them into the ranks of defense and guard?" Your foolish servant considers that although garrison troops are not natives, once they have been accustomed to the place for a long time, they naturally become comfortable with the local climate and terrain; and although farmers do not know martial arts, if they are trained with proper method, they too can naturally be made to take up arms. If those who serve as generals instruct them in military methods and nurture their keen spirit, causing the rhythms of sitting, rising, striking, and thrusting to become familiar through prolonged practice, and their resolute spirit of hostility toward the enemy to be roused when rendering service, then all such farmers and garrison soldiers can be made courageous and deployed into the ranks of defense and guard—just as in antiquity, when military levies drawn from land taxes were sufficient for use. Why worry, then, that the rank and file will not exert their strength? Since fields are fertile or barren, offer encouragement or punishment according to the abundance or scarcity of their yield; since harvests are plentiful or lean, exercise economy in proportion to the year's intake. When much effort is applied, barren fields can become fertile; when expenditure is carefully regulated, lean years will not lead to starvation. How then could one fail to secure grain and store it up in granaries, like the ancient…

之各異苟能時其水草而不失夫秣飼之宜謹
其孕字而不妨夫畜牧之利又何以不能致其
息而充溢於邊鄙若古之騋牝三千者歟是則
馬之蕃息食之贏餘士卒之練習實皆由於將
之得人而將之得人又本乎
皇上知人善任使也夫崇文德以安乎內而使中國
之尊安修武備以攘乎外而使四夷之賓服皆
已斷自
宸衷措諸政治其效驗之昭著如日月之光華天下
===
之所共覩矣尚何俟愚臣之言哉
皇上之策臣者臣既畧陳之矣伏讀
制策終篇有曰朕祗承
祖宗大統惓惓以經國子民為心而於安內攘外尤
加意焉臣有以見
皇上此心即古聖王兢兢業業憂勤惕厲之心也所
以崇文德者在是所以修武功者在是所以躋
斯世於雍熙泰和之域者亦在是所以四三王
而六五帝者又無不在是矣尚何用他求哉臣願
皇上永懷是心則治道之盛光于天下傳于萬世誠

之「萬億及秭」者歟？土地氣候有不齊，產息牧放之各異，苟能時其水草而不失夫秣飼之宜，謹其孕字而不妨夫畜牧之利，又何以不能致其息而充溢於邊鄙，若古之「騋牝三千」者歟？是則馬之蕃息、食之贏餘、士卒之練習，實皆由於將之得人；而將之得人，又本乎皇上知人善任使也。

夫崇文德以安乎內，而使中國之尊安；修武備以攘乎外，而使四夷之賓服，皆已斷自宸衷，措諸政治，其效驗之昭著，如日月之光華，天下之所共覩矣，尚何俟愚臣之言哉？皇上之策臣者，臣既畧陳之矣。伏讀制策終篇有曰：「朕祗承祖宗大統，惓惓以經國子民為心，而於安內攘外尤加意焉。」臣有以見皇上此心，即古聖王兢兢業業、憂勤惕厲之心也。所以崇文德者在是，所以修武功者在是，所以躋斯世於雍熙泰和之域者亦在是，所以四三王而六五帝者又無不在是矣，尚何用他求哉？臣願皇上永懷是心，則治道之盛，光于天下，傳于萬世，誠
translation_en:
… the ancient “tens of thousands of millions and hundreds of millions”? Where soils and climates are unequal, breeding and pasturing differ accordingly; yet if one can time their water and grass so as not to lose what is proper for foddering and feeding, and guard their pregnancy and foaling so as not to hinder the benefits of husbandry, why then could we not bring about their multiplication until they fill the frontier regions, like the ancient “tall mares numbering three thousand”? Thus the flourishing multiplication of horses, the surplus of food, and the training of soldiers all truly depend upon obtaining the right men as generals; and obtaining the right men as generals in turn is rooted in Your Majesty’s knowing men and employing them well.

Now exalting civil virtue in order to pacify the interior, thereby making the Central Lands honored and secure, and cultivating military preparedness in order to repel the exterior, thereby making the fourfold barbarians submit in allegiance—all these have already been decided from the Imperial heart and put into effect in governance. The manifest brilliance of their efficacy is like the radiance of the sun and moon, witnessed by all under Heaven alike; what need is there to wait upon the words of Your foolish servant? What Your Majesty has asked of Your servant in the policy question, Your servant has already briefly set forth. Humbly reading the conclusion of the Imperial policy question, where it says: “We respectfully繼 [succeed to] the great succession of Our Ancestors, earnestly taking the ordering of the state and thecherishing of the people as Our heart, and paying special heed to pacifying the interior and repelling the exterior”—Your servant can see that this heart of Your Majesty is none other than the cautious, conscientious, anxious, diligent, and vigilant heart of the ancient sage-kings. That whereby civil virtue is exalted lies herein; that whereby martial achievement is cultivated lies herein; that whereby this age is raised to the realm of harmonious splendor and supreme peace also lies herein; and that whereby one becomes a fourth to the Three Kings and a sixth to the Five Emperors likewise lies altogether herein. What need is there to seek elsewhere? Your servant wishes that Your Majesty may forever cherish this heart; then the flourishing of the way of governance will shine throughout the realm and be transmitted for ten thousand generations, truly …

translation_en: …boundless good fortune for the ancestral altars and the common people. Your servant's shallow and meager talent is insufficient for broad mastery of antiquity, and my stubbornly narrow learning is insufficient to comprehend the present. Offering the words of a mere grass-cutter and firewood-gatherer, I soil the Sagely Perusal above; if only Your Majesty takes pity on my foolishness and selects from them, I shall be fortunate beyond measure. Your servant has offended the Heavenly Majesty and is trembling to the utmost. Your servant respectfully replies.

title: 正統十三年進士登科錄
text:
臣岳正
臣對臣聞聖人之治本於道聖人之道本於中
蓋道者治之原中者道之體道以中而立治由
道而成苟治不本於道固無以成其治之盛道
不本於中又何以為道之大哉肆古之人君修
安內攘外之治者未有不本於兹也是故堯舜
禹以精一執中之道而為安內攘外之本則有
八元八愷之舉九官十二牧之命卒成萬邦咸
寧四夷来王之功商湯周武以建中建極之道
而為安內攘外之原則有天道人紀之修列爵
===
重教之政卒致四方徯予九夷通道之效則是
中之施於爵賞而爵賞宜施於刑罰而刑罰當
內治之綱豈有不舉者乎施於選將而將得其
人施於練兵而兵得其用外攘之本豈有不固
者乎此帝王之世所以安內攘外而康濟斯世
於雍熙泰和之盛者皆不外乎是中也恭惟
皇帝陛下聰明先物睿智有臨德為帝範道立民極
心同乎二帝三王之中治臻於二帝三王之盛
然猶不恃其道之已至而自足功之已成而自滿
萬幾之暇乃進臣等於

punctuated:
臣岳正。

臣對：臣聞聖人之治本於道，聖人之道本於中。蓋道者，治之原；中者，道之體。道以中而立，治由道而成。苟治不本於道，固無以成其治之盛；道不本於中，又何以為道之大哉？肆古之人君，修安內攘外之治者，未有不本於兹也。是故堯、舜、禹以精一執中之道，而為安內攘外之本，則有八元、八愷之舉，九官、十二牧之命，卒成萬邦咸寧、四夷来王之功；商湯、周武以建中建極之道，而為安內攘外之原，則有天道人紀之修，列爵重教之政，卒致四方徯予、九夷通道之效。則是中之施於爵賞而爵賞宜，施於刑罰而刑罰當，內治之綱豈有不舉者乎？施於選將而將得其人，施於練兵而兵得其用，外攘之本豈有不固者乎？此帝王之世所以安內攘外，而康濟斯世於雍熙泰和之盛者，皆不外乎是中也。恭惟皇帝陛下，聰明先物，睿智有臨，德為帝範，道立民極，心同乎二帝三王之中，治臻於二帝三王之盛。然猶不恃其道之已至而自足、功之已成而自滿，萬幾之暇，乃進臣等於
translation_en:
Your servant Yue Zheng 岳正.

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that the governance of the sages is rooted in the Way, and the Way of the sages is rooted in the Mean (zhong). For the Way is the source of governance, and the Mean is the substance of the Way. The Way is established through the Mean, and governance is accomplished through the Way. If governance is not rooted in the Way, there is certainly no means to achieve the flourishing of governance; if the Way is not rooted in the Mean, how then could it be the greatness of the Way? Therefore, among the rulers of antiquity who cultivated the governance of pacifying the interior and repelling the exterior, there were none who did not take this as their root. Thus Yao, Shun, and Yu took the Way of being discerning and undivided in holding fast to the Mean as the foundation for pacifying the interior and repelling the exterior; consequently there was the promotion of the Eight Worthies (ba yuan) and Eight Harmonies (ba kai), and the appointment of the Nine Offices and Twelve Pastors, ultimately accomplishing the achievement of all states being at peace and the four surrounding barbarian peoples coming to pay homage as to their king. Tang of Shang and Wu of Zhou took the Way of establishing the Mean and establishing the Supreme Standard as the source for pacifying the interior and repelling the exterior; consequently there was the cultivation of the Way of Heaven and human moral order, and the administration of ranking titles of nobility and emphasizing education, ultimately bringing about the effect of the four quarters waiting for them and the nine barbarian tribes opening up roads of communication. Thus, when this Mean is applied to ranks and rewards, ranks and rewards are fitting; when applied to punishments and penalties, punishments and penalties are proper—how could the guiding threads of internal governance fail to be upheld? When applied to selecting generals, the right men are obtained as generals; when applied to training troops, the troops are made effective in their use—how could the foundation of repelling the exterior fail to be secure? That whereby the ages of the Emperors and Kings pacified the interior and repelled the exterior, bringing peace and relief to this world in the flourishing of harmonious prosperity and supreme peace, was never anything outside of this Mean. Reverently I reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor, whose keen intelligence anticipates all things and whose profound wisdom oversees all, whose virtue serves as the model for emperors and whose Way establishes the standard for the people, has a mind identical with the Mean of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, and a governance reaching the flourishing of the Two Emperors and Three Kings. Yet You still do not presume upon Your Way having already reached its utmost to be self-satisfied, nor upon Your achievements having already been completed to be complacent. In the leisure from Your myriad affairs of state, You have summoned Your servants to…

title: 正統十三年進士登科錄
text:
廷策以安内攘外之務臣愚以為方今之治名器
必惜而爵賞無冗及之私鞭扑必慎而刑罰無
枉濫之失四海之内無不康乂矣而内治之政
夫復何修紀律有法而朝無不選之将教閲有
方而營無不練之兵萬方之遠罔不賓服矣而
外攘之功夫復何舉兹盖
陛下屈己下問虛心求道不忽葑菲之賤而擇芻蕘
之微即帝堯舍己從人帝舜好問好察湯文用
人惟己望道未見之盛心也臣雖愚昧敢不百
拜稽首以對揚
===
明命之萬一乎臣惟亮采惠疇皆所以修内治之
政也而爵賞刑罰為之綱戰守攻伐皆所以舉
外攘之功也而選将練兵為之本振其綱則目
舉培其本則枝茂此理之必然也
陛下以是而策臣愚臣愚有以知
陛下探治體之大以先務為急真不世出之主大有
為之君也臣請因
制策所及而槩陳之是故禄位車服者爵賞也然
必待有功而錫之則凡善有諸己而未著於事
功者賞有所不及是天下有遺善矣流宥鞭扑

政也而爵賞刑罰為之綱戰守攻伐皆所以舉
外攘之功也而選將練兵為之本振其綱則目
舉培其本則枝茂此理之必然也
陛下以是而策〔臣〕愚〔臣〕愚有以知
陛下探治體之大以先務為急眞不世出之主大有
為之君也〔臣〕請因
制策所及而槩陳之是故祿位車服者爵賞也槩
必待有功而錫之則凡善有諸己而未著於事
功者賞有所不及是天下有遺善矣流宥鞭朴
punctuated:
廷，策以安内攘外之務。臣愚以為方今之治，名器必惜而爵賞無冗及之私，鞭扑必慎而刑罰無枉濫之失，四海之内無不康乂矣，而内治之政夫復何修？紀律有法而朝無不選之将，教閲有方而營無不練之兵，萬方之遠罔不賓服矣，而外攘之功夫復何舉？兹盖陛下屈己下問，虛心求道，不忽葑菲之賤，而擇芻蕘之微，即帝堯舍己從人、帝舜好問好察、湯文用人惟己、望道未見之盛心也。臣雖愚昧，敢不百拜稽首，以對揚明命之萬一乎？

臣惟亮采惠疇，皆所以修内治之政也，而爵賞刑罰為之綱；戰守攻伐，皆所以舉外攘之功也，而選将練兵為之本。振其綱則目舉，培其本則枝茂，此理之必然也。陛下以是而策臣愚，臣愚有以知陛下探治體之大，以先務為急，真不世出之主、大有為之君也。臣請因制策所及而槩陳之。是故禄位車服者，爵賞也；然必待有功而錫之，則凡善有諸己而未著於事功者，賞有所不及，是天下有遺善矣。流宥鞭扑

… the court, questioning us in this policy examination on the urgent tasks of pacifying the interior and repelling external threats. In your foolish servant's view, in the governance of the present day, titles and ritual insignia are unfailingly cherished so that ranks and rewards suffer from no favoritism of superfluous bestowal, and the whip and rod are unfailingly applied with caution so that punishments and penalties suffer from no errors of injustice or excess. Within the four seas all are peaceful and well-governed—what more, then, needs to be cultivated in the administration of internal governance? Military discipline is regulated by law so that the court has no unvetted generals, and training and reviews are conducted with proper method so that the camps have no untrained soldiers. The myriad distant regions all submit in allegiance—what more, then, needs to be undertaken in the achievement of repelling external threats? This is because Your Majesty humbles yourself to inquire of your inferiors and empties your mind to seek the Way, not disregarding the lowliness of turnips and radishes and selecting from the humble words of grass-cutters and firewood-gatherers. This is truly the magnificent mind of Emperor Yao setting aside his own views to follow others, of Emperor Shun loving to question and loving to examine, of Tang using others as though their abilities were his own, and of King Wen gazing toward the Way as though he had not yet seen it. Though your servant is foolish and ignorant, how could he dare not bow his head to the ground a hundred times to respond to and extol even one ten-thousandth of Your illustrious mandate?

Your servant reflects that assisting in official affairs and順following the categories of governance are all means to cultivate the administration of internal governance, and that ranks, rewards, punishments, and penalties serve as their headrope; warfare, defense, attack, and chastisement are all means to accomplish the achievement of repelling external threats, and that selecting generals and training soldiers serve as their root. When one shakes the headrope, the meshes open; when one nourishes the root, the branches flourish—this is the inevitable course of principle. From the fact that Your Majesty questions your foolish servant on these matters, your foolish servant has the means to know that Your Majesty probes the great essentials of the body politic and treats the foremost tasks as urgent—truly a ruler who appears but once in generations, a sovereign of great achievements! 者刑罰也然必待有罪而施之凡惡存諸身而
未見於罪戾者罰有所苟免是天下有遺惡矣
古之聖王為是慮也無間於功與善而必賞之
以爵則凡有善於巳者皆得受上賞不但賞及
有功而巳若虞書三德為大夫六德為諸侯之
類是也無間於罪與惡而均罰之以刑則凡有
惡於巳者皆得有所警不但罰及有罪而巳若
王制行偽言偽以疑眾殺之類是也為人上者
誠能明德以為勸善之本則天下之人莫不是
則是效相觀而化如中庸所謂不賞而勸不怒
===
而威矣又奚待於爵之賞哉慎罰以為懲惡之
原則天下之人莫不是懲是創相戒以私如洪
範所謂遵王之道遵王之路矣又奚待夫刑之
罰哉夫爵賞刑罰勸善化惡內治之政雖不一
無非此中之流行也至若兵之所統者將將之
所用者卒是將與卒為軍旅之本矣卒之所仰
者食戰之所資者馬是食與馬為軍旅之用矣
昔之君子為是圖也以謂將其卒當選其卒之
良然豪傑之局於行伍也殽之以智愚蔽之以
妬忌未易知其才能而拔置軍旅之上也誠用

… constitute corporal and penal punishments. Yet if one must wait until there is a crime before inflicting them, then for all those who harbor evil in their persons without it yet manifesting in criminal offenses, punishment will be improperly escaped, and thus there will be unpunished evil in the world. The sage-kings of antiquity took thought for this: making no distinction between merit and goodness, they invariably rewarded them with rank, so that all who possessed goodness in themselves were able to receive high rewards, and rewards did not merely reach those with overt merit alone—such as "those of three virtues become Grand Masters, and those of six virtues become Feudal Lords" in the Book of Yu (Yushu), and the like. Making no distinction between crime and evil, they equally punished them with penalties, so that all who possessed evil in themselves were made to take warning, and punishments did not merely reach those with overt crimes alone—such as "those whose conduct is deceitful and whose words are false so as to mislead the multitude, put to death" in the Royal Regulations (Wangzhi), and the like. If one who stands above others can truly manifest bright virtue as the foundation for encouraging goodness, then among the people of the world none will fail to take this as their rule and model, observing one another and being transformed, just as the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) says, "Without rewards the people are encouraged; without anger they are awed"—what need, then, to wait for rewards of rank? And if he is cautious with punishments as the source for deterring evil, then among the people of the world none will fail to be deterred and chastened by this, warning one another against partiality and selfishness, just as the Great Plan (Hongfan) says, "Follow the King's way, follow the King's road"—what need, then, to wait for the penalties of punishment? Indeed, although the measures of internal governance—ranks and rewards, punishments and penalties, encouraging goodness and transforming evil—are not uniform, none is anything other than the flowing forth of this Equilibrium.

As for military forces, those who command the troops are the generals, and those whom the generals employ are the soldiers; thus generals and soldiers are the foundation of the army. What the soldiers rely upon is food, and what warfare depends upon is horses; thus food and horses are the practical resources of the army. When noble men of the past planned for this, they held that to command the soldiers one ought to select the best among them; yet when heroic men are confined within the ranks, mixed together the wise with the foolish and obscured by jealousy and envy, it is not easy to recognize their talents and abilities and elevate them to the head of the army. text:
孔子舉爾所知之言而求之則彼將拔茅連茹
而彙征矣戍其地當用其地之人然兵農既混
於一方也服介胄者非土著之安事耒耜者昧
干戈之習未易作其勇而驅列禦衞之間也誠
用仲由可使有勇知方之道而教之則彼將親
上死長而効力矣田有肥瘠嵗有豐歉必欲戰
其野則食其野之粟亦有其道誠使任屯種之
吏如漢武之用趙充國屯西羌則播藝有方畜
斂有法粟之所致必庾翼其多不患其不積貯
倉廩矣土地有厚薄氣候有寒暄必欲守其國
===

周孝之用秦非子牧汧渭則飲食有時調服有

鄙矣夫選將練兵足食牧馬外攘之功雖不同
無非此中之運用也是中也堯舜文武用之於

To garrison a region, one ought to employ the people of that region. Yet since soldiers and farmers are mingled together in a single locality, those who wear armor do not enjoy the settled peace of natives, while those who work with plowshares are ignorant of the practice of shields and spears; it is not easy to rouse their courage and drive them into the ranks of defense and guard. If we truly employ Zhong You's (Zilu's) Way of "making them have courage and know right conduct" to instruct them, then they will be devoted to their superiors, die for their leaders, and exert their utmost strength. If we truly entrust officials in charge of state-farm cultivation, just as Emperor Wu of Han employed Zhao Chongguo [Note: historically under Emperor Xuan of Han] to establish farming colonies in the Western Qiang region, then sowing and planting will have a proper method, and storing and harvesting will follow a regular system; the grain brought in will surely stand in stacks and rows in great abundance, and there will be no worry that it will not be accumulated and stored in the granaries. Soils vary in richness and thinness, and climates vary in cold and warmth; if one insists on defending a region and riding the horses of that region, how could there be no proper method for it? title: 正統十三年進士登科錄
text:
內攘外為急臣有以知
陛下兢兢業業夙夜弗遑安不忘危治不忘亂之所
發也足以四三皇足以六五帝而超軼於漢唐
宋之上矣臣愚學不足以博古識不足以通今
其於安內攘外之道盲乎有所未知徒以草茅
之言上瀆
天聽而自知有負
陛下之期待矣然於終篇竊有獻焉夫天地覆載之
無偏者天地之中也日月照臨之無私者日月
之中也帝王好惡之公刑賞之當德同天地明
===
並日月亦惟以其中耳是中也非聲音笑貌之
所能為必學之至行之力而後可造其極也臣
愚伏願
陛下萬幾之暇日引儒臣碩士講明是中之體擴充
是中之用則心與理會理與心融使堯舜禹精
一執中之道由是而得於心商湯周武建中建
極之道由是而措於事若然則爵賞刑罰選將
練兵之際無往而不適其宜推之家國天下九
夷八蠻無往而不從其化足以媲美帝王熈皞
之治茂隆

translation_en: …pacifying the interior and repelling the exterior as urgent tasks. Your servant thus knows that this springs from Your Majesty's cautious and diligent devotion, taking no rest from dawn to night, not forgetting danger in times of peace, nor forgetting disorder in times of good governance. This is sufficient to make a fourth with the Three Sovereigns and a sixth with the Five Emperors, surpassing the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties. Your servant is foolish; my learning is insufficient to comprehend antiquity broadly, and my insight is insufficient to understand the present thoroughly. Regarding the Way of pacifying the interior and repelling the exterior, I am as if blind and ignorant of it; I merely offer the words of a rustic scholar to impose upon Your Heavenly Hearing, knowing well that I have failed to live up to Your Majesty's expectations. Yet at the close of this essay, I humbly venture to offer a suggestion. Now, that by which Heaven and Earth cover and sustain all things without bias is the centrality of Heaven and Earth; that by which the sun and moon shine upon all things without selfishness is the centrality of the sun and moon. When an emperor or king is impartial in his likes and dislikes and fitting in his punishments and rewards, his virtue equals Heaven and Earth and his brilliance matches the sun and moon—this too is solely by virtue of his centrality. This centrality is not something that can be achieved through mere tone of voice or smiling countenance; one must reach the utmost in learning and exert oneself to the fullest in practice before one can attain its pinnacle. Your foolish servant humbly hopes that Your Majesty, in the leisure from Your myriad affairs of state, will daily summon Confucian officials and eminent scholars to elucidate the substance of this centrality and expand the application of this centrality, so that the mind and principle meet, and principle and the mind merge as one. Thus, the Way of Yao, Shun, and Yu—of being refined and single-minded and holding fast to the Mean—will thereby be grasped in the mind; and the Way of Tang of Shang and Wu of Zhou—of establishing the Mean and establishing the Supreme Standard—will thereby be put into practice in affairs. If this is so, then in bestowing ranks, rewards, punishments, and penalties, and in selecting generals and training troops, there will be nothing that does not suit what is proper; extended to the family, the state, and all under Heaven, as well as the Nine Yi and Eight Man tribes, there will be none who do not submit to its transforming influence. This will be sufficient to rival the prosperous and harmonious governance of the ancient emperors and kings, and to grandly exalt…

title: 正統十三年進士登科錄
text:
宗社悠久之福此臣犬馬之忠惓惓有望於
陛下也若夫騁浮夸以自衒非臣之素志矣惟
陛下少垂
睿覽則愚臣幸甚天下幸甚臣冒干
天威不勝戰慄之至臣謹對

punctuated: 宗社悠久之福。此臣犬馬之忠，惓惓有望於陛下也。若夫騁浮夸以自衒，非臣之素志矣。惟陛下少垂睿覽，則愚臣幸甚，天下幸甚。臣冒干天威，不勝戰慄之至。臣謹對。
translation_en: … the enduring blessings of the ancestral altars and altars of soil and grain. This is the earnest hope that your servant, in his humble loyalty, holds for Your Majesty. As for indulging in empty bombast to show off myself, that has never been your servant's lifelong aspiration. If only Your Majesty will deign to cast Your imperial gaze upon this, your foolish servant will be most fortunate, and all under Heaven will be most fortunate. Having presumed to offend the Imperial Majesty, your servant is overcome with trembling and awe. Your servant respectfully replies.
